_note: Slate for the Roof (decision 0485): Dorcas Brigham, the carter from Cooper's Ford, on the meetinghouse roof at Harlow Bridge. Drafts for Matt. Her voice is the road's: loud, says exactly what she thinks, keeps her counts. Facts are in docs/regions/harlow-bridge.md and old-post-road.md.

lines.text: You. You were at the ford, standing about with the rest of us.
I was.
Well, it moved in the end. Sixty squares, and I've laid all but the last three bundles.
The mill hands were handing up all morning. Then the wheel went, and so did they.
Pass me the rest off that pile. Mind the edges. They'll cut you.
Off the pile and up the ladder. I'm not coming down for it.
Eldwin passes a bundle of slate up the ladder. It's heavier than it looks.
That's one. Don't stand under me.
Madam, I could sing you up the rest of it. The roofers in the old country swore by it.
I'll swear by it too, if you start.
Eldwin passes up another bundle.
Good slate. Splits clean.
Course it does. I don't carry rubbish.
Two. You're quicker than the mill hands.
Is that a goose?
She's with me.
Keep her off my ladder.
Eldwin passes up the last bundle.
And that's sixty. That's the roof.
She comes down the ladder backwards, quicker than she went up.
Sixty squares, and not one cracked.
She looks at the meetinghouse door for a while.
Two days on top of it. I suppose I'd better see what I've been keeping the rain off.
I'm going. Don't rush me.
Dorcas is at the back, just sitting down on the end of the last pew. She looks up.
Well! It's bigger from underneath.
It comes back down at her off the ceiling.
You want to keep your voice down in a church. Nobody tells you that.
